proposals.name: Au Gres-Sims School District Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
Shall
the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Au Gres­-Sims School District, Arenac County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 1.18 mills ($1.18 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 10 years, 2026 to 2035 inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the construction or repair of school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall
the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Au Gres­-Sims School District, Arenac County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 1.18 mills ($1.18 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 10 years, 2026 to 2035 inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the construction or repair of school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and for all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2026 is approximately $376,824?
proposals.officialTitle: Au Gres-Sims School District Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 1.18 mills for 10 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.

proposals.description:
It
is proposed that Standish Township levy a tax of 1.00 Mill. The proposed millage includes (1) a renewal of 0.9955 mill that was previously approved by voters in 2022 and (2) an increase of 0.0045 mill as new additional millage. This renewal and increase would restore the Township's authority, which was reduced by law, to levy a total of 1.00 mill. The money raised would be used to fund the construction, preservation, improvements, repairs, and maintenance of the roads within Standish…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
It
is proposed that Standish Township levy a tax of 1.00 Mill. The proposed millage includes (1) a renewal of 0.9955 mill that was previously approved by voters in 2022 and (2) an increase of 0.0045 mill as new additional millage. This renewal and increase would restore the Township's authority, which was reduced by law, to levy a total of 1.00 mill. The money raised would be used to fund the construction, preservation, improvements, repairs, and maintenance of the roads within Standish Township. This would cost you about $1.00 for each $1,000.00 of your taxable real and personal property. The charge would apply each year from 2026 through 2029, inclusive. Approximately $64,773.48 would be raised in the first year. Should the proposed renewal and increase be approved?
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 1 mill for 2026–2029 — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.description:

proposals.ballotLanguage:
This millage proposal would allow Standish Township to levy 1.00 Mill for the purpose of reducing and controlling the mosquito population within Standish Township. 
Shall Standish Township, Arenac County, Michigan, increase the limitation on the total amount of general ad valorem taxes which may be imposed for all purposes in Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, as amended, by 1.00 Mill ($1.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for a period of four (4) years (2026 through 2029, inclusive), which would provide an estimated revenue of $64,773.48 in its first year if approved and levied, for the purpose of reducing and controlling the mosquito population within Standish Township. Should the proposed millage increase be approved?

proposals.name: Road Brining Millage
proposals.description: Shall the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution of General Ad Valorem Taxes within Turner Township, Arenac County, Michigan, be renewed at up to 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for a period of four years (2027 to 2030) inclusively for the purpose of the brining of Turner Township roads? If levied, this millage would raise approximately $35,000 in the first year.
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution of General Ad Valorem Taxes within Turner Township, Arenac County, Michigan, be renewed at up to 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for a period of four years (2027 to 2030) inclusively for the purpose of the brining of Turner Township roads? If levied, this millage would raise approximately $35,000 in the first year.
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 1 mill for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.name: Au Gres-Sims School District Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
Shall
the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Au Gres­-Sims School District, Arenac County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 1.18 mills ($1.18 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 10 years, 2026 to 2035 inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the construction or repair of school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall
the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Au Gres­-Sims School District, Arenac County, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 1.18 mills ($1.18 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 10 years, 2026 to 2035 inclusive, to create a sinking fund for the construction or repair of school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and for all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2026 is approximately $376,824?
proposals.officialTitle: Au Gres-Sims School District Sinking Fund Millage Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 1.18 mills for 10 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.
